title: Weakly etale algebras over a field
statement:
If $k$ is a field and $B/k$ is weakly etale
[def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], every finitely generated $k$-subalgebra of
$B$ is finite etale. In particular $B$ is ind-etale, is reduced, and all its
residue fields are separable algebraic over $k$.

proof.text: Every $k$-module is free after choosing a basis, and hence flat: tensoring a direct sum of copies of $k$ preserves injections coordinatewise. Thus the common flat-resolution bound over $k$ is zero. Apply the common-bound conclusion of [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-tor] to $k\to B$: every $B$-module is flat. Fix a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-ring-weakly-etale] and composition in [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], $k\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is weakly etale; the same Tor-bound argument shows every $B_{\mathfrak q}$-module is flat.

source.place: Tag 092Q (lemma-absolutely-flat-over-field), first two proof paragraphs; zero-bound argument is the blueprint first paragraph

proof.text: Put $C=B_{\mathfrak q}$, a local ring by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. For a nonunit $b\in C$, the quotient $C/(b)$ is flat by step 1. Apply [lem-exc-flat-quotient-element-equation] to find $e\in(b)$ with $b=be$. Since $b$ lies in the maximal ideal so does $e$, whereas $1-e$ is a unit; hence $b(1-e)=0$ forces $b=0$. Thus every nonzero element is a unit, and $C$ is a field. Its maximal ideal is zero, so $B_{\mathfrak q}=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$.

source.place: Tag 092F (lemma-absolutely-flat), local-field argument expanded using Algebra Tag 04PS

proof.text: If $x\in B$ is nilpotent, its image in each field $B_{\mathfrak q}$ vanishes. The fraction equality defining localization says that for each $\mathfrak q$ some $s\notin\mathfrak q$ has $sx=0$. If $x\ne0$, its annihilator is a proper ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-over-proper-ideal] it is contained in a prime $\mathfrak q$, contradicting the preceding $s$. Thus $B$ is reduced. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-field-separable] to the weakly etale field extension $k\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ from steps 1-2: every residue field of $B$ is separable algebraic over $k$.

Let $A\subseteq B$ be a finitely generated $k$-subalgebra. It is reduced, since a nilpotent in $A$ is nilpotent in $B$. Let $\mathfrak p$ be a minimal prime of $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-injective-minimal-prime-lift] choose $\mathfrak q\subset B$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$. The map $A\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ has kernel $\mathfrak p$: elements of $\mathfrak q$ map into the zero maximal ideal of this field; conversely if $a/1=0$, some $s\notin\mathfrak q$ kills $a$, so primeness gives $a\in\mathfrak q$. Consequently $A/\mathfrak p$ embeds in the separable algebraic field $B_{\mathfrak q}$. It is itself a field: for $0\ne a\in A/\mathfrak p$, a minimal-degree polynomial relation over $k$ has nonzero constant coefficient (otherwise cancel $a$ in the domain), and solving the relation expresses $a^{-1}$ as a polynomial in $a$. Hence $\mathfrak p$ is maximal. The same injection shows every element of this field is separable over $k$, since its minimal polynomial is unchanged by an injective $k$-algebra map.

source.place: Tag 092Q (lemma-absolutely-flat-over-field), minimal-prime paragraph, using Algebra Tag 00FK

proof.text: Every ideal of the field $k$ is either zero or the whole ring, so $k$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $A$ is Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes] gives finitely many minimal primes. Every prime of $A$ contains a minimal prime by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime]; since the latter is maximal by step 4, these primes are equal. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is finite. Apply [pqf-lem-finite-type-algebra-finite-spectrum] to obtain that $A$ is finite-dimensional over $k$.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions] for the reduced Noetherian ring $A$: its total ring of fractions is the finite product of the fields $A_{\mathfrak p}$ at its minimal primes. Every nonzerodivisor $a\in A$ is a unit. Indeed, by [lem-pc-minimal-prime-avoids-nonzerodivisor] it belongs to no minimal prime; all primes are minimal by step 5. If $(a)$ were proper, [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-over-proper-ideal] would give a prime containing $a$, a contradiction. Thus all denominators in the total ring of fractions are already units, and $A\cong Q(A)\cong\prod_{\mathfrak p} A_{\mathfrak p}$ as $k$-algebras. Since $\mathfrak p$ is maximal and $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is a field, $A/\mathfrak p\to A_{\mathfrak p}$ is an isomorphism: the quotient is a field and every localization fraction is the image of the quotient numerator divided by its nonzero quotient denominator. By step 4 these factors are separable over $k$, and by step 5 they are finite-dimensional (quotients of $A$). Apply [lem-sc-finite-etale-algebra-criterion]: $A$ is finite etale over $k$.

source.place: Tag 092Q (lemma-absolutely-flat-over-field), final decomposition paragraph; decomposition via Algebra Tags 02LX and 00U3

proof.text: The finitely generated $k$-subalgebras of $B$ form a set directed by inclusion: the subalgebra generated by the union of two finite generating sets contains both. Their union is $B$, because every $b$ lies in $k[b]$. This directed union is their filtered colimit as $k$-algebras: compatible algebra maps on the subalgebras define a unique map on $B$, with operations respected by passing finitely many elements to a common subalgebra. Each term is finite etale by step 6. The definition [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] therefore makes $B$ ind-etale. If $B=0$, the subalgebra diagram consists of the zero algebra, the field and prime arguments above have no instances, and the decomposition is the empty product; all conclusions hold.
